==English== ===Etymology=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*kʷ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|who}}, {{m|enm|hwo}}, {{m|enm|huo}}, {{m|enm|wha}}, {{m|enm|hwoa}}, {{m|enm|hwa}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hwā}} (dative {{m|ang|hwām}}, genitive {{m|ang|hwæs}}), from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*hwaʀ}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*hwaz}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kʷos}}, {{m|ine-pro|*kʷís}}. The sound change {{IPAchar|/hw/}} > {{IPAchar|/h/}} (without a corresponding change in spelling) was due to [[w:Wh-cluster reductions|''wh''-cluster reduction]] after an irregular change of {{IPAchar|/ɑː/}} to {{IPAchar|/oː/}} in Middle English (instead of the expected {{IPAchar|/ɔː/}}) and further to {{IPAchar|/uː/}} regularly in Early Modern English. A similar change occurred in {{m|en|two}}. Compare {{m|en|how}}, which underwent ''wh''-reduction earlier (in Old English), and thus is spelt with ''h''. Compare {{cog|sco|wha}}, {{cog|fy|wa}}, {{cog|nl|wie}}, {{cog|nds|we}}, {{cog|de|wer}}, {{cog|sv|vem}}, {{cog|da|hvem}}, {{cog|nb|hvem}}, {{cog|nn|kven}}, {{cog|is|hver}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|ho͞o}} * {{IPA|en|/huː/|a=RP,Wales}} * {{IPA|en|/hʉw/|a=SSB}} ** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Back ache-who.wav|a=London}} ** {{audio|en|En-uk-who.ogg|a=London}} * {{IPA|en|/hu/|a=GA,CA}} ** {{audio|en|En-us-who.ogg|a=California}} * {{IPA|en|/hʉː/|a=AU,NZ}} * {{IPA|en|/hʉ/|a=Scotland,NI}} ** {{rhymes|en|uː|s=1}} * {{enPR|h(w)o͞o, h(w)ō|a=Early Modern}}, {{IPA|en|/h(w)uː/|/h(w)ɔː/|/hwɒ/|q3=originally unstressed}}{{R:en:Dobson:1957|II|153|677}} * {{homophones|en|Hu}} ===Pronoun=== {{en-pron|desc=singular or plural, nominative case|objective|[[whom]], [[who]]|possessive|whose}} # {{lb|en|interrogative}} What person or people; which person or people; {{n-g|asks for the identity of someone; used in a direct or indirect question}}. #: ''You're [[get married|getting married]][[‽]] '''Who''' to?'' (direct question) #: ''I don't know '''who''' it is.'' (indirect question) #: {{ux|en|'''Who''' says they care? —They themselves do.}} #: {{ux|en|'''Who''' does she wish (that) I'd married.}} #: {{ux|en|'''Who''' is coming to your party? Marry to. ---- Come Captaine, will you goe? ''Oth''[''ello'']. Ha, with '''who'''?}} #* {{quote-video game|en|developer=w:BioWare|title={{w|Mass Effect (video game)|Mass Effect}}|location=Redwood City|publisher=Electronic Arts|year=2008|genre=[[science fiction|Science Fiction]]|system=PC|scene=Citadel|isbn=9780784546642|oclc=246633669|passage=Chorban: I don't really think my scanning disturbs them, but the authorities might disagree.
Chorban: I'd like to do it more openly, but it's not really worth getting arrested over.
Shepard: I could help you out. I'm not worried about the authorities.
Chorban: I don't even know '''who''' you are.}} # {{sid|en|relative clause}} {{lb|en|relative}} {{n-g|Introduces a relative clause having a human antecedent}}. ## {{n-g|With antecedent as subject.}} ##: ''That's the man '''who''' works at the newsagent.'' (defining) ##: ''My sister, '''who''' works in the accounts department, just got promoted to manager.'' (non-defining) ##: {{ux|en|an email from my sister, '''who''' I hope will be fully recovered soon}} ##* {{quote-av |en |date=July 18, 2026 |quotee=Kat |time=0:40 |title=Charlotte residents rally against ICE killings across the country |publisher=w:WCNC-TV |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260719131411/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pZTsDqtva0w |platform=w:YouTube |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pZTsDqtva0w |archivedate=July 19, 2026 |text=Yeah, so we just want to stand with our immigrant community, uh we note that our neighbors are being killed by ICE and there's no accountability, there's no justice; so we just want to stand with them here and note that they're not alone and that there's people '''who''' support them.}} ## {{lb|en|non-formal}} {{n-g|With antecedent as object}}: [[whom]]. ##: {{ux|en|That's the man '''who''' I saw earlier.|q=''defining''}} ##: {{ux|en|My brother, '''who''' you met the other day, is coming to stay for the weekend.|q=''non-defining''}} # {{lb|en|fused relative|archaic|or|marginal}} [[whoever|Whoever]], he who, they who. #: {{ux|en|'''Who''' dares wins.}} #: {{ux|en|'''Who''' insults my mother insults me.}} #: {{ux|en|Give it to '''who''' deserves it.|q=''marginal usage''}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Othello|III|3|text='''Who''' steals my purse steals trash.}} # {{lb|en|informal|especially|non-US}} {{n-g|Also used with names of collective nouns that are groups of people, especially singularly-named musical groups or sports teams.}} #: {{ux|en|'''Who''' are the {{w|Miami Heat|Miami Heat}}?}} ====Usage notes==== {{U:en:who and whom}} * When ''who'' (or the other relative pronouns ''[[that]]'' and ''[[which]]'') is used as the subject of a relative clause, the verb typically agrees with the antecedent of the pronoun.
